---
title: "Figures and Quarto"
subtitle: "Wrapping a table in a float, and the show rule a long one needs."
description: "How to put a Keisen table inside a Typst figure, why a figure stops it breaking, and how to emit one under Quarto."
---

`display-table` returns a table, never a figure.
Wrapping is the caller's job, which leaves numbering, captions, and cross-references with whoever owns the document.

```typst
#figure(
  display-table(sales, table-stub(rowname: "product")),
  caption: [Regional sales for the year.],
  kind: table,
) <tbl-sales>
```

**A figure does not break across pages.**
`breakable: true` is the default here, and it has no effect inside a figure until this is in force:

```typst
#show figure: set block(breakable: true)
```

This is the first thing anyone hits with a long table: the table stops breaking the moment it is wrapped, and nothing about the wrapping says so.
Typst also places figure captions below by default, so a table caption usually wants moving to the top with a show rule.

`table-header` and a figure caption are alternatives, not partners.
An in-table title is the `gt` house style; a caption is numbered and can be referenced.
Using both prints the title twice.

Under Quarto, emit the table alone and let Quarto own the float:

````markdown
::: {#tbl-sales}

```{=typst}
#display-table(sales, table-stub(rowname: "product"))
```

Regional sales for the year.

:::
````

Hand-rolling `#figure` inside a raw Typst block fights Quarto's cross-reference system, which is what the enclosing div is for.

A very wide table is the caller's problem too, solved with `rotate(reflow: true)` around it or a flipped page.
The package assumes nothing about page geometry, so it survives either.
